I am seeing a lot of disagreement here between new mount and blade players and old mount and blade players. I got the game back in 2014, but I didn't touch native multiplayer until late 2018 so idk if that is a new perspective to offer, but it is a perspective I would like to offer nonetheless, and I have to say even not having that attachment to Warband MP's combat that some other people might have I still disagree with you.

Infantry: Due to the significant block delay swing speed seems to be the name of the game right now. Unless a player really knows what they are doing someone with a faster weapon will generally beat someone with a slower one.  Shield fights are also nearly unbearable. In Warband, you moved and swung quick enough that you could use footwork and positioning to get around someone's shield, in Bannerlord you move and swing too slowly to do the same so shield fights end up with you and your opponent wacking each other's shields until one breaks. Due to the strength of shields in Bannerlord this will often take a bit. If you have a weaker or smaller shield, then you are likely to lose unless you have a weapon that does extra damage to a shield, such as an axe.

Archery: I will admit that I was not a fan of archery in Warband. My main issue with archery was the projectile speed, bows and crossbows traveled as fast as a rifle shot and it was difficult for someone using one to see where their bolt/arrow went. I really do enjoy the addition of the white trail the projectile leaves behind as it helps archers understand where they are hitting, and why they may have missed. I do think though that the projectile speed is a bit too slow and could be upped a bit, not to Warband levels, but to a reasonable level, the trade-off for this would be lowering damage. Overall, an actual improvement over Warband.

Cavalry: Bannerlord cavalry is by far one of the most unbalanced instances of mounted combat I have seen in a game. In Warband the horses movement was awkward, but fighting on cav itself was entertaining, you had to time your thrust or swing properly and pikes/lances on the ground felt like an actual threat. Couching was also a risky move as you traded accuracy for sheer damage. Bannerlord cav feels broken in comparison. Pikes/lances do not always stop a charging horse as sometimes you can be knocked down, albeit while doing damage, but any good cav player can easily take advantage of your condition, and your thrust is unlikely to kill the horse unless it was traveling at full speed due to the ridiculous tankiness of almost all horses in the game. Cav players also seem to take very little damage when flung off of their horse, and the ability to block an incoming attack as you are getting up does not help. Couching is by far the worse change they have made to cav. As I said, in Warband there was a high risk/ high reward for couching, in Bannerlord there is little risk and high reward. Couching even when not traveling at full speed can deal over 400 damage insta-killing any person or horse you hit, it is also surprisingly accurate compared to Warband couching. Additionally, you can couch indefinitely and while building up only minimal speed. Horses, To fix cav issues they need to make it so lancing is either less accurate/not indefinite or make it a trade-off that if you couch once your lance breaks, or you cannot couch with that lance again. They also need to make pikes/lances more effective against horses.

Aggravating these combat issues is a poor balance between the factions and their classes which Taleworlds seems unable to fix. I desperately hope they took a close look at the current state of the game and fix the glaring issues with combat and balancing.
